title: Deployment dry-run checklist and safety-belt notes
content:
Purpose:
- Quick personal playbook for the upcoming dry-run (non-prod) of model rollout + routing change. Not the final runbook — this is my scratchpad for what to watch and operators to ping if things go south.

Goals (what I want to validate in the dry-run):
- End-to-end routing from API -> region pool -> model variant completed without errors.
- KV cache priming leads to improved p50 for long-context prompts.
- Autoscale bump logic triggers correctly under simulated burst.
- Rollout signal thresholds (latency/error/cost) are sane and actionable.
- Rollback and fallback paths operate within <5 minutes from detection to full revert.

Assumptions:
- Dry-run executes in staging cluster (eu-west-1 test pool).
- We will route 5% of synthetic traffic from lead QA jobs only.
- Model variant: model-x-2q (quantized) pinned for experiment.
- KV priming will use cached prefixes from sample prompt set (see PR 987).

Quick checklist (pre-run):
- [ ] Confirm PR merged and image tagged: runtime:release-2024-11-05-priming
- [ ] Fill ticket PROD-3421 with run plan + participants
- [ ] Notify SRE on-call and set incident bridge (Zoom/Slack huddle) 10m before start
- [ ] Ensure dashboard widgets for the run exist (latency, errors, token-cost, qps per model)
- [ ] Create ephemeral alert rule: staging/p50>300ms for 5m OR error-rate>1% for 3m
- [ ] Load KV prime data into test cache cluster (run: tools/kv-prime --file sample-prefixes.json)

Rollout sequence (dry-run):
1) 00:00 — baseline snapshot: take metrics for 15m window (p50/p95 latency, 5xx, cost/token)
2) 00:15 — push model variant to staging pool (0% traffic) and do smoke GETs from sdks/clients
3) 00:25 — route 1% test traffic via feature flag (ff:deploy.dryrun.2024-11-12)
4) 00:40 — ramp to 5% synthetic traffic, monitor for 20m
5) 01:00 — run autoscale burst test (simulate 3x qps) and watch instance spin-up
6) 01:15 — roll forward to 10% only if metrics OK; otherwise hold and escalate

Metrics & thresholds (staging targets + what to alarm on):
- Latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms (staging is looser than prod)
- Errors: 5xx rate < 0.5% ( >1% triggers immediate hold )
- Token cost: average cost/token should not increase >20% compared to baseline
- Mem/CPU on instances: no instance >90% sustained for 2m
- KV cache hit-rate: target > 60% after priming

Primary failure modes and quick actions:
- Error spike (5xx >1%): pause traffic ramp, revert routing rule to previous model tag, notify SRE and runtime owners, capture traces (traces/logs link in dashboard).
- Latency regression (p95 > 500ms): reduce concurrency, enable fallback variant (model-x-2q-fallback) and step traffic back to 0.
- Autoscale failure (no new instances within 90s): abort ramp, set manual capacity bump (console -> dedicated pools -> add 2 nodes), escalate to infra on-call.
- Cache warmup not effective: abort priming, clear test cache and re-run prime with larger sample set.

Rollback commands (staging, manual quick revert):
- Revert routing via console: routing -> edit policy -> set model = model-x-1q-stable -> save
- CLI: redwoodctl rollout set --route staging-api --model model-x-1q-stable --force-replace
- If instance-level revert: kubectl -n staging rollout undo deployment/runtime-serving --to-revision=<prev>

Observability checklist (what I will watch closely):
- Dashboard: staging/route/model-x-2q -> latency panel, 5xx panel, traces link
- Logs: sample errors -> grep for "kv-cache-miss" and "oom"
- Traces: check tail latencies on generate_tokens spans
- Cost: quick check on token cost dashboard and per-token break-down (unexpected spikes are suspicious)

Test prompts & qualitative checks (what QA runs manually):
- Prompt set A: long-context multi-turn (5 prompts) — check coherency and hallucination rate
- Prompt set B: short completions under 64 tokens — check latency & completions similarity to baseline
- Prompt set C: embedding baseline (sanity) — make sure embedding dimension and cosine scores stable
- Human check: have Samira run 10 manual sessions and annotate any out-of-scope answers

Communication plan: who to ping and when
- Pre-run: post plan in #deploys 30m prior, @here in #deploys 5m prior
- On anomaly: call SRE on-call, tag @runtime-team, open incident in PROD-3421
- Post-run: short summary in #deploys + update PROD-3421 with snapshots and decisions

Open questions / TODOs (my personal list):
- Q: Do we want to enable prefix-level cache merging across pods for this experiment? Pros/cons need quick doc.
- TODO: ask Infra about ephemeral node warmup time in staging (Ethan)
- TODO: measure token-cost behavior with quantized model in longer sessions (Priya)
- Done: PR 987 merged but need sample prompt refresh (Samira to confirm)

Notes from quick dry-run on 2024-10-29 (learning):
- KV prime gave ~30% p50 improvement for long-context but only 10% p95 improvement — indicates tail still dominated by IO
- Autoscale reacted slower than expected in one test where qps jumped 4x; added a 60s pre-warm hook to scale policy (needs verification)
- Observability gaps: no direct token-cost per-request metric for staged pool; added a short-term probe that tags requests with cost estimate (PR link above)

Post-run artifacts to attach (after live dry-run):
- metrics-snapshot-YYYYMMDD.csv
- trace-sample-<timestamp>.json
- short-postmortem-notes.md (if any anomaly)

Final personal safety note: keep the manual rollback steps at hand in a separate tab, and give SRE the explicit permission to cut traffic if they see threshold breaches. If anything feels ambiguous, stop ramp and escalate early.

End of scratchpad — will convert to a proper runbook after one more dry-run iteration.
